column1: # WHY A BASELINE AND NOT A FIX: every entry below is a PRE-EXISTING trap on this tree. The

# ⛔ WHAT THIS FILE DOES NOT DO: a count may FALL freely and the gate stays green, so a
# SCAN LOSS (a span that stopped being read) is grandfathered too until the row is re-emitted.

# A count may FALL freely; it may not RISE (a rise is a new trap, and it reds).

portability-baseline: pre-existing on the tree this PR lands on, NOT yet repaired — both sites (`:875`, `:890`) are a GNU-first/BSD-second `sed -i` ladder on ONE line: `sed -i "…" f 2>/dev/null || sed -i '' "…" f`, so the BSD suffix form is the fallback arm, not a bare BSD-only call. Landed on main in `217237888` AFTER this baseline's last touch, so it is main-owned rather than a trap this change introduced. The single portable form is `sed -i.bak -e … && rm -f f.bak`, or `box_sed_i` (scripts/lib/box.sh).

portability-baseline: DELIBERATE GNU-FIRST ordering — `stat -c %Y` must come before BSD `stat -f %m` (agent-infra#1702: under GNU coreutils a BSD-first arm never runs, because `-f` reads as filesystem-status and prints a filesystem block while exiting 0). The BSD arm is on the next line and a `case ''|*[!0-9]*` guard discards a non-numeric read.

portability-baseline: 5 live sites, and they are NOT all one shape. FOUR are GNU-first arms of documented ladders with their BSD `stat -f` arm on the next line (`:1021` %W birth, `:1023` and `:2388` %Z ctime, `:2718` %Y mtime). The FIFTH (`:1692`) is a procfs-only %Y read guarded by `[ -r "$REAP_WT_PROC_ROOT/$pid" ]` whose fallback is `ps -o etimes=`, NOT a BSD `stat` arm — do not read it as a ladder. `box_mtime` is a valid repair for %Y (`:1692`, `:2718`) only; birth (%W) and ctime (%Z) have no shim. This count was 2 before the +3 that landed 2026-11-01 (`e83d41a1`) and were never baselined.
